heading: EXT. HOLLOW OF THE SINGING STONES - TWILIGHT

units.text: EXT. HOLLOW OF THE SINGING STONES - TWILIGHT
A bowl in the mountains ringed with standing stones as tall as barns.
The stones hum, each on its own faint note, and the notes braid together into something almost like speech.
Mist pools in the hollow.
Violet light bleeds from the west.
Four travelers have come down the goat path into the circle.
QUILLON ASHDOWN, thirties, a lean scout with a bow across his back, kneels to touch the turf.
MAEVE OKONKWO-FAIR, twenties, a healer in a moss-green cloak, stands with one hand on the nearest stone and her eyes shut.

Behind them, the old knight SIR GERVASE THORNWICK, sixties, leans on his greatsword, wheezing from the climb, and his squire, little DOBBIN, twelve, hugs the sword's scabbard and stares up at the stones with a mouth like a small round O.
The stones sing a little louder.
Quillon draws an arrow, thinks better of it, and slides it back into the quiver.
Maeve opens her eyes and takes her hand from the rock as if it had burned her.
Sir Gervase straightens, and Dobbin drops the scabbard, picks it up again, and drops it again as the hum climbs a half-step.
Maeve. What are they saying?
units.name: QUILLON

units.text: They aren't saying. They're remembering.
units.name: MAEVE

units.text: Remembering what?
units.name: QUILLON

units.text: Everyone who has ever stood here.
units.name: MAEVE

units.text: That would be a long list.
units.name: SIR GERVASE

units.text: It is.
units.name: MAEVE

units.text: Dobbin steps to the center of the circle, where a flat, dark stone lies embedded in the grass like a coin.
He crouches and traces a groove in it with one finger.
Sir Gervase, there's writing.
units.name: DOBBIN

units.text: Can you read it, lad?
units.name: SIR GERVASE

units.text: Not all of it. It says something about a door.
units.name: DOBBIN

units.text: A door?
units.name: QUILLON

units.text: "Speak the name of the one you have lost, and the door will open."
units.name: DOBBIN

units.text: Silence.
The stones fall quiet all at once.
The mist stops moving.
Maeve looks at Quillon.
Quillon looks at the grass.
Sir Gervase studies his sword.
Dobbin glances from face to face.
Who goes first?
units.name: DOBBIN

units.text: Nobody answers.
A wind lifts the edge of Maeve's cloak and lets it fall.
Quillon wipes his palms down his thighs.
At last Sir Gervase clears his throat, sets the sword point-down in the turf, and bows his head.
Ysolde.
units.name: SIR GERVASE

units.text: The stones sing once, a single bright note, and the dark stone in the center brightens to the color of an ember.
Quillon swallows.
Maeve shuts her eyes again.
Dobbin takes Sir Gervase's free hand, and the old knight lets him.
Quillon.
units.name: MAEVE

units.text: I know.
units.name: QUILLON

units.text: Say it.
units.name: MAEVE

units.text: I can't.
units.name: QUILLON

units.text: You can.
units.name: MAEVE

units.text: Tamsyn.
units.name: QUILLON

units.text: The ember brightens.
A seam of light opens in the air above the stone, thin as a thread, and the whole hollow leans toward it.
Maeve steps forward, then Dobbin, then Sir Gervase with his sword on his shoulder, and Quillon last, and the door in the air widens until it is the size of a man.
